newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians form committees to combat settlements.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians form committees to combat settlements.

text.p: The Palestinian Authority said on Friday it had formed committees to combat Israeli settlement policy in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
"The Palestinian people are going to defend their land strongly and firmly against the cancerous settlements," said Palestinian official Ahmed Abd Al-Rahman after the weekly cabinet meeting.
"We formed committees in the Palestinian towns and villages to defend our land," he said, adding the committees would provide financial, political and legal support to local residents.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu enraged Palestinians when he lifted a four-year freeze on Jewish settlement construction in occupied Arab land shortly after his right-wing Likud party came to power in June.
Palestinians view Jewish settlements in territories where they hope to build an independent state as a provocation and oppose any increase in their numbers.
"We will start from Saturday surveying the areas which are threatened by settlements in order to take the necessary steps," said Palestinian Finance Minister Mohamad Zuhdi Nashashibi.
Some 130,000 Jews have settled amidst more than two million Palestinians since Israel seized the West Bank and Gaza in 1967.

Netanyahu has approved the construction of thousands of new homes for Jews in the West Bank since August. But, much to the chagrin of settler groups that helped him come to power, he has not gone ahead with plans for new settlements.

Under a 1993 Israel-PLO peace deal, the fate of Jewish settlements will be determined in talks on a final peace accord to be completed by 1999, along with other thorny issues such as borders between Israel and a future Palestinian entity.
